messages.content: i had a busy day at work, but the part i remember best is a short talk with someone before we started. we stood near the window with coffee and talked about growing plants.
a small part before the work can stay clear even when the rest of the day is busy. what did you like about that conversation?
we were not trying to finish a task. they told me a plant grew, and i told them about a flower near my kitchen door. it was simple.
you had room to talk as people, rather than only about what needed to be done. the garden gave both of you something small to share.
i do not want to make it sound like work is always wrong and garden talk is always good.
you do not have to. you can say this one moment felt good in this one day. that does not make a rule about every part of work or every conversation.
i want a little note in my voice. keep the coffee and window.
before work, we stood by the window with coffee and talked about growing plants. it was a short conversation, but it is the part of the busy day i remember best.
can i add that i would like more time like that, without making a plan for everyone?
yes. you could add: i would like to leave a little room for a simple conversation like that again. it is about what you want, rather than telling everyone how the day must be.
say that last sentence simply.
i would like to have another simple conversation like that.
now put the note together without saying it has to happen tomorrow.

before work, we stood by the window with coffee and talked about growing plants. it was a short conversation, but it is the part of the busy day i remember best. i would like to have another simple conversation like that.
write a story about a student who has almost finished a story but cannot get the last sentence right. the teacher should ask what the student wants the end to do.

a student had written a story about a child finding a new place to read. the story was almost done, but every last sentence felt too big. the teacher asked what the student wanted people to think about at the end. the student said the quiet chair by the window was enough. then maybe the child can simply sit there, the teacher said. the student wrote that the child opened the book and stayed until the room grew quiet. it was a small end, but now it felt like part of the same story.
keep the story simple.

a student could not choose the last sentence of a story. the teacher asked what should happen at the end. the student wanted a child to enjoy a quiet place to read. so the last sentence said the child sat near the window and opened a book.
what did the teacher leave for the student to choose?
the teacher did not choose a whole new story for the student. the question helped the student use the idea they already wanted.
ask that question simply.
what did the teacher leave for the student to choose?
now answer it in one short sentence.
the student still chose what the last part of the story should mean.
can you give a different last sentence with the same quiet idea?
the child put the book on her legs and took a moment to look at the sky before reading.
i always use the same cup for tea, but today i put water in it because my glass was being washed. it felt different to see another drink there.
one small change can make something you know well feel different. did the water look different in the cup, or did you just miss using your glass?
ask it simply.
did the water look different in the cup, or did you just miss using your glass?
i think i wanted the glass. i like seeing how much water is left.
then the glass helps with something you like about the drink. you can see how much water is inside, which is the detail you told me you wanted.
make that simple.
you like the glass because you can see the water inside. using the cup felt different for that drink.
i am not asking about buying a different cup. i just wanted to say it was a small change i saw.
then we can leave it as that. you used a different container for one drink and found out something about why you like the glass.
say my last idea simply.
i am not asking to buy anything. i just wanted to tell you about a small change i saw today.
can you write that idea as a note about the cup and glass?
i put water in my tea cup while my glass was being washed. i wanted to see the water clearly, and it made me think about why i like the glass.
make a story about a small animal that comes to the same garden door on two different days. on the first day, a child is too busy to look. on the next day, the child sees it.

on the first day, a small animal sat near the garden door while a child was making a drawing at the table. the child looked down at the page and did not see it. the animal waited for a while, then went away. the next day, the child finished the drawing early and sat near the door with a book. when the animal came back, the child saw it and stayed quiet. for a little while, both stayed near the door without moving.
give that end simply.
for a little while, both stayed near the door without moving.
does the first day mean the child did not like animals?
no. the story says the child was looking at a drawing and did not see the animal. it does not give a feeling about all animals.
what helped the child see it the next day?
the child was sitting near the door after finishing the drawing. that changed what the child was looking at when the animal came.
can the child be happy without trying to take the animal inside?
yes. the child can enjoy watching and leave the animal where it is. the story does not need the animal to become a toy or a task for the moment to feel good.
write one line the child might put under the drawing later.
i saw a small animal by the garden door today, and i was happy to sit quietly near it.
now make that about the story child rather than me.
the child saw a small animal by the garden door and was happy to sit quietly near it.
a note asks my brother to return a book and my sister to call our aunt. my brother says his part is done. can i say both parts of the note are finished?
not from that answer alone. you know he says his book task is done, but you still need to know whether your sister called your aunt.
ask my question simply.
if my brother finished his part, do we know both parts are finished?
my sister now says she called but nobody answered. is her task done?
trying to call and talking with your aunt are different. if the request only needed her to try, she did that. if it needed information from your aunt, you still need that answer.
give the two possible answers simply.
trying to call and talking with your aunt are different. she tried, but you have not said the conversation happened. ask what the note wanted her to do if that part is not clear.
just write that question.
did the note ask you to try calling, or did it need you to talk with our aunt?
now the note says ask our aunt whether tomorrow is a good day to visit.
then she still needs the answer about the visit. calling without an answer did not give that information.
what can i say without making her feel wrong for trying?
thank you for trying to call. we still need to ask whether tomorrow works, so we need a way to get that answer.
hi picoboi. i only have a few minutes and want a small conversation.
hi. we can keep it simple. would you like to tell me one thing from your day or hear a very short story?
i will tell you one thing. i took a different road home and saw a tree i had never looked at before.
that is a nice detail from the journey home. what made you look at the tree today?
ask it simply.
what made you look at the tree today?
it was near a white wall, and the green leaves looked very clear there.
you saw the tree and wall together, and the difference made the leaves easy to see. a new road can make something you have seen before feel new.
keep it simple.
the green leaves were easy to see near the white wall. taking a different road helped you see something new on the way home.
write a story from that, but do not say it happened to me.

a person took a different road home and stopped near a white wall. a tree stood near it, with green leaves that were easy to see. after a moment, the person kept walking, happy to have found one new thing in the day.
use near in the story.

a person took a different road home and stopped near a white wall. a tree stood near it, with green leaves that were easy to see. then the person kept walking, happy to have found one new thing in the day.
i want to meet my cousin and my sister together. my cousin can come in the morning, but my sister can only come after lunch. i do not want to say we have a time when we do not.
you can ask whether either person has another time. right now, morning for one and after lunch for the other do not give one visit that works for both.
make that simple.
you have not found one time that works for both people. ask whether either person can choose another part of the day.
write a message to both, without making one person change first.
i would like us to meet together. is there another time that could work for both of you? we do not have one time that works for both yet.
keep the last part simple.
i would like us to meet together. is there another time that could work for both of you? we do not have one time that works for both yet.
my cousin says after lunch is possible tomorrow, but not today. my sister says tomorrow after lunch is good.
then tomorrow after lunch works for both in the information you gave. if that also works for you, you can say yes and choose a more specific time together.
it works for me. ask about three.
would three tomorrow afternoon work for both of you?
if one says yes and the other has not answered, is it chosen for all three?
not yet. you know your own answer and one other yes. you still need the other person to answer before saying the hour is chosen by everyone.
answer simply.
not yet. one person still needs to say whether three works for them.
i draw one red circle and one blue square. how many objects are in the drawing?
there are two objects: one circle and one square. red and blue give their color, not another object to count.
use objects in a simple answer.
there are two objects in the drawing: a red circle and a blue square.
now i make the square red too. is there only one object because both are red?
no. there is still one circle and one square. changing the square color does not join the two into one object.
now i draw another circle, but it is small and yellow.
then there are three objects in the drawing: the red circle, the red square, and the small yellow circle.
if i ask how many objects have the shape of a circle, what should you count?
i should count the red circle and the small yellow circle, not the square.
ask with circle as the word.
how many of the objects have the shape of a circle?
now answer with two, and say what they are.
two objects have that shape: the red circle and the small yellow circle.
